name: tabor-ark-of-the-covenant
title: The Ark of the covenant
description: The KJV construction account and the trail through its later appearances.
sections: The instructions specify shittim wood, gold overlay, rings and staves, the mercy seat and two cherubims. Exodus gives dimensions of two and a half by one and a half by one and a half cubits.
Exodus names Bezaleel as builder and records the construction of the Ark, its carrying staves and its mercy seat.
The Philistines take the Ark from Ebenezer to Ashdod and place it in the house of Dagon.
The Ark arrives on a cart. The Levites take it down and set it on a stone.
The Ark is brought into Abinadab’s house and his son Eleazar is set apart to keep it.
David brings the Ark from the house of Obededom and sets it in the pitched tabernacle.
Josiah instructs the Levites to put the Ark in the house that Solomon built. The verse records the instruction.
The narrative records the transfer of the Ark into the oracle of Solomon’s temple.
Hebrews names the manna pot, Aaron’s budding rod and the tables in its description of the tabernacle. The Solomon dedication account in 1 Kings 8:9 gives the two tables in the Ark at that point.
2 Maccabees gives an account of Jeremiah sealing the Ark, tabernacle and altar of incense in a cave on the mountain Moses climbed. A modern location remains unverified.
The Ethiopian Orthodox tradition credits Menelik with bringing the Ark from Jerusalem to Aksum. Smithsonian’s account records the tradition and the guardian’s restrictions on viewing.
Keep each later custody claim attached to its earliest identifiable text and any independent evidence for the object’s identity.
